sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Explains why old and new bands differ
sections.what: The header comment explains that the newer rule raised confidence without new evidence, which narrowed every band that had evidence. It names the two constants this module uses: the superseded agreement factor and the widening floor.
sections.why: The comment warns that a reader who sees tighter ranges may wrongly infer more certainty, so the module makes the cause explicit.
sections.watch_out: The comment does not repeat computed figures because they change. Do not add new numbers to the prose.

sections.name: wideningFactor
sections.title: Calculates how wide a range gets
sections.what: Returns a widening factor from a confidence value. Lower confidence gives a larger factor, so a range is wider. This section also defines the tolerance used when comparing with the engine.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the comments. The comment says it follows the specification's widening formula.
sections.watch_out: The floor must match the engine. A change to only one side is not caught here.

sections.name: BandComparison
sections.title: Record of one process's band comparison
sections.what: Describes one process's comparison: its confidence under both rules, its factors, the change, whether it has evidence, and any disagreement message.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely reason: the page shows old and new side by side.
sections.watch_out: The disagreement message is the only signal that the two sources differ, so the page must display it.

sections.name: ComparableProcess
sections.title: Inputs needed for band comparison
sections.what: Describes the four pieces of data needed for each process: its id, confidence, the engine's widening factor and whether it has evidence.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the comment. The comment says the viewer compares against the engine and does not invent the value.

sections.name: compareBands
sections.title: Builds the old-versus-new band table
sections.what: For each process, recalculates the factor under both rules, compares the recalculated factor with the engine's stored factor, flags any disagreement, computes the change from the engine's factor, and sorts the results by process id.
sections.why: The comment says reading the stored value and also recalculating it means a changed constant cannot pass unnoticed.
sections.watch_out: The change is taken from the engine's factor. If the two factors disagree, the percentage and the recalculated figure will not match.

sections.name: narrowingTracksEvidence
sections.title: Checks narrowing matches evidence
sections.what: Returns true only when every process whose range narrowed had evidence, and every process whose range held still had none. If it returns false, the page should drop the claim and show a warning.
sections.why: The comment says the claim that narrowing followed existing evidence should only be shown when the pattern actually holds.
sections.watch_out: One process that breaks the pattern removes the claim from the page entirely, which is intentional.

summary: Recalculates how wide each process's effort range is under the current rule and the older 2.0.0 rule, checks the result against the engine's stored value, and produces the comparison shown to readers.
purpose: Explains why ranges look narrower in the current version than in an older deliverable, without implying that new evidence was found.
why: The header comment says the narrowing is a correction of an old penalty, not a discovery. Readers who see tighter ranges could wrongly infer more certainty, so the comparison is shown explicitly.
how: A widening factor is calculated from confidence with a fixed floor. The module computes the factor under the current confidence and under a confidence scaled by the older constant. It compares its own factor with the engine's stored factor and flags any disagreement beyond a small tolerance. Finally it checks whether every process whose range narrowed had evidence, and every process that did not narrow had none.
inputs: A list of processes, each with confidence, the engine's widening factor and an evidenced flag.
outputs: A sorted list of comparisons, one per process, with both factors, the percentage change, any disagreement message, and a true or false result for the evidence pattern.
risks: The floor value is copied by hand from the engine, so a change in only one place goes unnoticed. The change figure is taken from the engine's factor, so it can differ from the recalculated one if they disagree. A false pattern result hides the claim without a clear error.
debug: If a range looks wrong, compare the engine's stored widening factor with the value this module recalculates. If the page shows a divergence message, check the engine's floor and the confidence value. If the claim disappears, check the evidence pattern result.
